Klamath and Salmon River War of 1855 and its aftermath

A regional historical topic linked here for Karuk, Yurok, and Hupa context. The Klamath River is a place name here; this is not a study of the Klamath people of Oregon. Relevance must be assessed source by source.

Umatilla culture, history and timeline

Owner-supplied Umatilla study. Distinguish Umatilla people, the CTUIR government and its Cayuse and Walla Walla constituent peoples. Broader Columbia River material needs its own community and historical scope. Bibliographic labels are supplied leads, not original-source inspection.

20 links · Open Umatilla’s collection →

Walla Walla culture, history and timeline

Owner-supplied Walla Walla study. Distinguish Walla Walla people from CTUIR government, Cayuse and Umatilla constituent peoples, and the modern city. Broader Columbia River sources need their own historical/community scope. Supplied bibliography labels are leads, not original-source review.

24 links · Open Walla Walla’s collection →

Tillamook culture, history and timeline

Owner-supplied Tillamook study. Keep Tillamook people and historical language, individual coastal communities, Clatsop/Nehalem relationships, and the distinct Siletz and Grand Ronde governments in their stated contexts. Supplied bibliography labels are leads, not original-source review.

23 links · Open Tillamook’s collection →

Squamish history, culture and timeline

Owner-supplied Squamish study. Distinguish Squamish people, Squamish Nation government, language and town; neighboring nations and shared institutions are not aliases. Original publications and cultural/access limits require review.
